newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu wants peace talks nearer home -son.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu wants peace talks nearer home -son.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko will not travel to South Africa this week for planned talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila on ending Zaire's civil war, his son and spokesman said on Monday.
"Apparently President Mobutu doesn't want to travel to South Africa. He prefers somewhere else," Nzanga Mobutu told Reuters. "It's a long flight and he's still convalescing."
Asked if Mobutu would prefer to go to Brazzaville, capital of neighbouring Congo across the river from Kinshasa, Nzanga said: "From what I've heard Kabila doesn't want to go to Brazzaville."
He said, however, that the talks were not off and that negotiators from both sides were still working on a date and venue.
Mobutu reluctantly agreed to meet Kabila, who demanded direct talks as a condition for ending his six-month-old armed campaign to topple the long-serving president.

Kabila's forces have seized more than half of Zaire's vast territory and are threatening to bring the war to the capital Kinshasa if Mobutu does not agree to step down at their planned meeting. Mobutu wants the talks to set the stage for elections.
